newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Av. price of NZ commodity exports falls in Jan-ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Av. price of NZ commodity exports falls in Jan-ANZ.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of New Zealand's commodity exports fell 0.6 percent in January following a 0.6 percent rise in December, ANZ Bank said on Monday.
ANZ said its commodity price index showed the corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports dropped 0.1 percent in January compared with a 0.2 percent rise in December.
It said the New Zealand dollar index declined to 99.0 in January from 99.6 in December, while the world price index fell to 123.7 from 123.8 over the same period.
On an annual basis, the New Zealand dollar index recorded a 10.3 percent fall in January while the world price index dropped by 3.6 percent.
"While January was a weak month for most of the commodities surveyed, prices remained particularly soft for wool, beef and forestry products," ANZ said.
"Strong prices for lamb prevailed during January providing some support for the NZD commodity price index, while prices for aluminium also showed a marked improvement over the month."
ANZ said the price of New Zealand's forestry exports had fallen steadily over the past year after maintaining firm levels during 1994 and 1995.

While the fall in the NZD forestry price index mirrored the decline in the index measured in world prices during the first half of 1996, the gap between the two indices had widened over the past six months.
"World forestry prices have been constrained by a strong cyclical downturn for pulp and paper and soft prices for logs in Japan," ANZ said.

It said the weakness in the NZD index had been compounded by the rise in the NZD especially against the Japanese Yen. In addition, New Zealand's forestry exports had a high exposure to markets in Japan and Australia, where weak residential construction activity over 1996 reinforced the downturn in log and sawn timber prices.
